title: VC-Dimension Dichotomy for Identifying Codes (Approximation)
statement_text: For any hereditary class of graphs $\mathcal{C}$, either (1) the minimum identifying code size has a logarithmic lower bound and Min Id Code is log-APX-hard in $\mathcal{C}$, or (2) the minimum identifying code size has a polynomial lower bound and Min Id Code admits a constant factor approximation algorithm in $\mathcal{C}$.
context_text: An identifying code of a graph $G$ is a set $C$ of vertices such that $N[v]\cap C\neq\emptyset$ for every vertex $v$ and $N[u]\cap C\neq N[v]\cap C$ for all distinct $u,v$, where $N[v]$ is the closed neighbourhood; it exists if and only if $G$ is twin-free (no two vertices with the same closed neighbourhood), and Min Id Code asks for one of minimum size $\mathrm{id}(G)$. Always $\mathrm{id}(G)\ge\log(n+1)$; Min Id Code is NP-complete and log-APX-hard in general (no $(1-\varepsilon)\log n$-approximation). A hereditary class is closed under induced subgraphs; 'logarithmic lower bound' means that the best lower bound on $\mathrm{id}$ in the class is $\Theta(\log n)$, while 'polynomial lower bound' means $\mathrm{id}(G)\ge n^{\varepsilon}$ for some $\varepsilon>0$ and all twin-free $G$ in the class. The VC-dimension of a graph is that of the hypergraph of its closed neighbourhoods (the largest vertex set $X$ such that every subset of $X$ is $N[v]\cap X$ for some $v$), and that of a class is the supremum over its members. The dichotomy is an informal pattern observed by the authors in the known results (split, bipartite, co-bipartite, chordal graphs on one side; line, planar, unit interval graphs on the other), not a conjecture they make. The paper settles it: the lower-bound half holds (classes of infinite VC-dimension contain arbitrarily large graphs with identifying codes of logarithmic size, while classes of VC-dimension $d$ have $\mathrm{id}(G)\ge(n-1)^{1/d}$), and Min Id Code is log-APX-hard in every hereditary class of infinite VC-dimension; but the approximation half is false: $C_4$-free bipartite graphs have VC-dimension $2$ and $\mathrm{id}(G)=\Theta(n^{1/2})$, yet Min Id Code cannot be approximated within $c\log n$ for some $c>0$ in this class unless $NP\subseteq ZTIME(n^{O(\log\log n)})$. The authors give a $6$-approximation for interval graphs; constant-factor approximability remains open for graphs of girth at least $5$, chordal bipartite graphs, unit disk graphs and undirected path graphs.
notes: The lower-bound half of the dichotomy is fully proved as Theorem 2.2. The approximation half is shown to fail in general: C4-free bipartite graphs have finite VC-dimension but Min Id Code cannot be approximated within a factor of c log|V| for some c > 0 (Thm 4.3). The question of which finite VC-dimension classes admit constant-factor approximations remains open (Table 2 lists Girth ≥ 5, Chordal bipartite, Unit disk, and Undirected path graphs as open).
